acceptanceCriteria: When a return trip ticket has a promo code discount, the discount amount is correctly included in the Mozio dispatch report (dispatch.report.price.discount.amount) before being passed to mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch
The promo code discount amount displayed in the Mozio email confirmation for a return trip ticket matches the expected discount value (same as shown for the equivalent one-way trip)
mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch correctly renders the discount.amount and discount.name for return trip dispatches without masking or dropping the amount value
handleTicketsNote in generate-staff-notes.helpers.ts correctly reflects the promo code discount amount (ticket.discount) for return trip tickets in staff notes
processZeroAmountOrderService correctly processes return trip orders where the promo code reduces the total to zero, without throwing UNEXPECTED_ORDER_PRICE
Existing one-way trip promo code discount display behavior is not regressed
after.description: When a promo code is applied to a return trip ticket, the discount amount is not displayed as expected in the Mozio email confirmation. The return-trip-specific code path in create-reservations.mappers.ts (getTripData with isReturnTrip flag) swaps from/to stations but may not correctly propagate the promo code discount amount into the dispatch report that feeds mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch and ultimately the email confirmation. Additionally, zero-amount return trip orders (where promo code covers full fare) must be handled correctly by processZeroAmountOrderService.
after.title: [Mozio] - Promo code amount not displayed for return trip tickets in Mozio email confirmation

notes: The bug is that promo code discount amount is not displayed correctly for return trip tickets in Mozio email confirmations. Tracing the code: create-reservations.mappers.ts handles return-trip-specific logic (swapping from/to stations via getTripData), and the discount amount flows through dispatch.report.price.discount into mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch which feeds the email. The discount is likely not being correctly propagated or calculated for return trip dispatches during reservation creation/submission. mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch passes discount.amount through as-is, so the root cause is upstream in how the dispatch report is built for return trips.

When mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch receives a return trip dispatch containing a discount, the output includes both discount.amount and discount.name with the correct values — neither field is omitted or zeroed out
Staff notes for return trip tickets with a promo code discount include the correct discount amount and discount name
When a promo code reduces a return trip order total to zero, the order is processed successfully without throwing an UNEXPECTED_ORDER_PRICE error
For one-way trip tickets with a promo code discount, the discount amount and name continue to display correctly in the Mozio email confirmation, dispatch report, and staff notes

When a return trip ticket has no promo code discount (discount is null, undefined, or zero), no discount amount or name appears in the Mozio email confirmation or dispatch report, matching the behavior of one-way trips without discounts

When a return trip ticket has a partial promo code discount (discount covers some but not all of the fare), both the discount amount and the remaining total price are correctly reflected in the Mozio email confirmation
When the discount object for a return trip dispatch is missing or malformed, the system does not crash and the email confirmation is still generated without a discount section

notes: Modified AC3 to remove implementation-leaning language ('renders', 'masking or dropping') and reworded as an observable outcome specifying what the output must contain. Modified AC4 to remove the specific file and function name (handleTicketsNote, generate-staff-notes.helpers.ts) and focus on the observable staff-notes content; also added discount name since the original only mentioned amount. Modified AC5 to remove the specific service name (processZeroAmountOrderService) and describe the observable behavior instead. Modified AC6 to be more specific about what 'not regressed' means — listing the three surfaces (email confirmation, dispatch report, staff notes) and both fields (amount and name). Added three new edge-case criteria: (7) return trips with no discount should behave identically to one-way trips with no discount, (8) partial discounts must show both discount and remaining total correctly, (9) missing/malformed discount data must not crash the system.
